# Naive momentum vs NIFTY benchmark — published TRI

*Generated by `python -m backtest.run --policy naive_momentum --benchmark-report`. The benchmark is read out of `L1/benchmark_tri` with `read_tri_series`, which prefers the exchange's **published** total-return series and falls back — loudly — to §4.1's computed estimate and then to a broad-market L1 basket. The heading above names which of the three this run actually got.*

## Benchmark provenance

- **Provenance:** `published_tri` — published TRI.
- **Series:** the **published** NIFTY TRI for `Nifty 50` (slug `nifty50`, method `published`) — `nifty_tri_history`, ingested by M3.9.b from `POST /BackPage/getTotalReturnIndexString`.
- **Path unchanged:** whichever series stands, it flows through the same `TriSeries` / `compare_to_benchmarks` machinery (M9.4 acceptance #3), so the provenance changes the series and nothing else about how the excess is computed.

## Window

- 2016-09-02 -> 2026-08-31 (2470 sessions, 120 monthly rebalances)
- Replay time: 62.3 s

## Return vs benchmark (money-weighted XIRR, identical cashflows)

| Series | XIRR |
| --- | --- |
| Portfolio (naive momentum, **costs included**) | 10.92% |
| Nifty 50 — published TRI (M3.9.b, `published`) | 11.92% |
| **Excess over benchmark** (published TRI) | -1.01% |

> **Benchmark provenance:** the benchmark is the **published** NIFTY total-return series for `Nifty 50` — `nifty_tri_history` as ingested by M3.9.b (`published`), read out of `L1/benchmark_tri` with `read_tri_series` and point-in-time to the terminal valuation. Excess over this is excess over the real benchmark. It is still not alpha: costs, survivorship of the traded universe and the single-path nature of one backtest all sit between the two.
